note: Inherited requirements with explicitly bounded source mappings. Mapping is not full language conformance. SCHEMA 2 (card T00-CT-SCHEMA, T00.1-T00.9): every per-case stage entry is an object whose status is derived from named executed evidence, not a host-unconditional string. An `executed` entry must name the `executor` (a pinned runner in compiler/tests/ct_corpus.rs), the `artifact` that runner reads (the case's own fixture), an `observations` count of runner invocations, and, where the runner is host-gated, the exact `host_gate` list of target_os values on which it runs; the harness recomputes all of that from its own dispatch and refuses any drift, so on a host outside the gate the entry reads as unexecuted instead of inheriting `executed`. Statuses are `executed`, `recorded_not_gated` (an archived transcript that no workspace test re-runs; it must carry a `record` pointer and can never be counted as executed), `not_applicable` (the stage is structurally absent for this route, or the case's own refusal provably never reaches it) and `unassessed`. `proof` is never `not_applicable`, because a bound theorem could be added for any case. `native_sanitized` is `not_applicable` on a route that has no `c_emission` stage and `unassessed` everywhere else: card T08-SRC-CT deliberately narrowed the earlier universal rule when the check-only `epoch` route landed, because there is nothing to sanitize where nothing is emitted, and the route vocabulary — not the case — decides it. SCHEMA 1's `cfg` and `type_checker` are gone: they conflated four real passes and their reading differed per route. The stage vocabulary now names the passes that exist (parse, elaborate, task_lowering, task_ledger_check, mutex_lowering, mutex_invariant_check, epoch_lowering, epoch_bound_check, sequential_whole_program, sequential_reference_execution, task_reference_execution, mutex_reference_execution, c_emission, native_execution, native_sanitized, legacy_c_twin, proof) and each case declares its `route`. A route's possible stages are listed under stage_vocabulary.routes; every stage outside them is structurally absent for that route. The task route (ScopedCopyTasksV1/ScopedOwnedTasksV1 and its ScopedReadSharesV1/ScopedErrorPayloadV1 extensions) builds a checked task IR, which is what schema 1's `cfg` meant there; the source.mutex.guard.v1 route (CT26/CT27/CT28/CT29/CT30/CT31/CT32/CT48) emits directly from a checked event list and has no CFG stage at all, which schema 1 could only express as `cfg: unassessed`. The source.epoch.bound.v1 route (CT35/CT36/CT38/CT39, cards T08-EPOCH-SRC and T08-SRC-CT) lowers a lexical epoch declaration onto the unedited FlatEpochBoundV1 checker and is check-only: an admitted epoch is a checked accounting statement about declared shapes, published with c_source: None and reference_observation: None, so it has no reference-execution, emission, native or sanitized stage at all. The legacy_c route (CT43/CT45, card CT-CTWIN) is the first non-QCore artifact in this corpus: both cases name C constructs — a registration API that defers a callback past its own return, and a destructor whose body is outside the translation unit — that no QCore syntax expresses, so the case's artifact is a C twin run through the real unrestricted-C gateway. On that route `parse` is the gateway's own C admission (validate_unrestricted_c11: Clang preprocessing plus syntax acceptance of the case's own .c bytes) and `legacy_c_twin` is analyze_unrestricted_c11's resource projection and unit verdict; there is no `elaborate` because there is no QCore source, and no emission, native or sanitized stage because the gateway analyzes C rather than producing any. The evidence is the whole verdict — unit result, verbatim withdrawal reason, complete per-function status map and complete ordered diagnostic inventory, each rebuilt from the analysis and compared wholesale — plus controls that remove exactly the construct the scenario names, at least one of which the gateway must check, so a recorded Unknown is never merely `the projection cannot express this at all`. That route's stages are gated on Clang rather than on a target_os, which the stage record carries as a new optional `tool_gate` beside `host_gate`; the derived summary reports it as a separate `tool_scope` axis, because a stage that reads `host_gate: null` and needs Clang would otherwise be read as having run wherever the tests ran. A control that varies only the declared contracts re-analyzes the case's own artifact and is therefore counted as a further observation of that case's own stage, which is the one deliberate exception to `a control is never the case's own stage`. The sequential route is declared and currently carries no mapped case. CT28/CT31/CT32/CT48 are the card T03-F additions (bounded task composition inside the guard profile, the `wait` announced acquisition, and guard-scoped facts); their accepted controls are route-checked, and for CT28/CT31/CT32 those controls are multi-task modules this backend cannot render in one thread, so they carry no native evidence and their `evidence_target` records the Q500 host gate rather than an executed run. Several unmapped cases have recorded reasons rather than absent evidence. CT11 asks for full permission reconstructed while local shared *aliases* survive; ScopedReadSharesV1 has no local alias form at all, and in the closest measured program the party retaining the share is an unjoined child task, so mapping it would answer a different question (card T05 section 9). CT06 needs an owned-pointer copy form the grammar does not admit. CT35/CT36/CT38/CT39 are now mapped on the epoch route (card T08-SRC-CT) after card T08-EPOCH-SRC supplied the source syntax; their accepted cases carry the epoch_bound_figures verdict mode, whose evidence is the exact published certificate rather than the bare verdict, because an epoch that merely checks has measured nothing. Every quantity on those certificates is a declared figure and the four FlatEpochBoundV1 premises are carried unchanged, so mapping these four adds no native, sanitized or proof evidence.

cases.scenario: Move an owned buffer to child; child returns it; parent joins and drops
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. Linux native allocation, pointer-preserving child return, creator join and exactly-once parent drop agree with reference execution. Loans, general owned graphs, owned errors and native runtime refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Parent uses buffer after successful move capture
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. The parent read after successful move rejects at Q600; CT01 supplies the accepted native control. Failed creation retains the original parent binding. Loans, general owned graphs, owned errors and native runtime refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Parent and child share reads with complementary positive shares
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: one owned Buffer lent to two children with complementary halves of the 1024-unit read authority, both reading it while the parent also reads it, and Buffer writes on either side of the lending window because a write demands reconstructed exclusive authority. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, all-paths task-IR check, reference execution, C11 emission, and three fixed Linux schedules whose emitted C runs under ASan/UBSan/LSan with a heap witness recording every Buffer by address - one object allocated and released exactly once across two live borrowers, a refused second creation returning only its own share, and a refused join returning none and reclaiming nothing. The complementary refusals are mapped as CT04 and CT05. This is not evidence about arbitrary schedules, other targets or the C memory model; ThreadSanitizer does not intercept C11 thrd_create, so data-race freedom rests on the checker's no-write-while-shared rule. The lending budget is over authority handed out, not a separation-logic fraction; disjoint slicing, write shares, more than two readers, byte accounting and nested workers stay refused.

cases.scenario: Parent writes while child retains a read share
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: the parent writes its Buffer while both children still hold their halves. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying LoanOutstanding { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, borrowers: [2, 3] }, which names the outstanding total and every borrower rather than the bare fact of a loan. An accepted Linux control moves the same write after both joins, so the refusal is keyed to the outstanding shares and not to writing at all. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.scenario: Two children each request FULL for the same memory
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: two children each request the whole read authority for one allocation. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying ShareExceedsAuthority { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, requested: 1024 }; the excess request is refused as a whole and the outstanding total is unchanged. An accepted Linux control lends 511 and 513 of the same allocation, so the budget boundary is a boundary rather than a blanket refusal of two borrowers. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.expected: Capture state restored; no task obligation
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. Injected native creation failure restores the original buffer binding for read/drop, with no child or join obligation. cases.scenario: Second create fails after first succeeds
cases.expected: First task must still be joined
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedCopyTasksV1 explicit creation recovery: real source matches the second spawn result. Failure preserves the first task until the Err arm explicitly joins its exact native thread, then returns42. Success joins both children and returns7; initial failure has no child. A failure arm omitting the prior join rejects with Q600 ScopeBusy. Reference and native outcomes agree for all3 fixture creation scripts. This tests scalar copies and task obligations, not owned/loan capture restoration, arbitrary handlers or other native platforms.

cases.scenario: Child finishes but parent has not joined
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1: the native adapter waits for the actual worker body and completion-record write before creation returns to the parent. Parent read/drop of the moved Buffer before join reject at Q600 despite worker completion. The accepted control joins, consumes the owned Result and drops the original generation. Exact pointers and join-before-reclamation checks retain the allocation and environment while completed but unjoined. This is one owned Buffer, not loan/share restoration or a general scheduler proof.

cases.scenario: Backend join failure
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedCopyTasksV1 native fault evidence: a real i32-copy worker is created; successful control joins then frees the environment and returns 42. An injected native join failure establishes no quiescence and aborts before result publication or environment reclamation. The fault is supplied only by a test runtime adapter. Reference execution covers the successful control; native join failure has no returning reference transition. No source-owned payload/loan restoration, full runtime refinement or other-platform native conformance is claimed.

cases.scenario: Worker typed error after partial local acquisition
cases.expected: Clean locals, return loans, carry declared payload
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1 worker-local allocation: a real child acquires up to two Buffers, explicitly drops all acquired locals before raising WorkerError::Failed or a bound AllocError, and the creator joins before receiving the error. Four native/reference scenarios cover success, either allocation failure and creation failure with exact pointer/thread checks. Missing cleanup in either worker error arm rejects at Q600. The earlier sequential implicit-cleanup control remains separately executed. Loans, owned error payloads, arbitrary handlers and native refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Worker error payload contains owned result
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedErrorPayloadV1: exactly one owned Buffer rides an explicitly tagged worker error out of one child, through its completion capsule and its creator's join, and is taken out of the bound error exactly once. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, all-paths task-IR check, reference execution, C11 emission, and five fixed Linux schedules whose emitted C runs under ASan/UBSan/LSan with a heap witness recording every Buffer by address - the success path releases all three objects inside the child, either worker allocation failure carries the parent's original identity back and releases every local it does not carry, a refused creation transfers nothing, and a refused join reclaims neither payload nor environment. Two negative controls pin that an undelivered payload and an unreleased taken payload are refused at Q600. One payload, one flat own<Buffer>: recursive owned graphs, several payloads, mixed declared rows, nested workers and loans inside payloads stay refused, and no race detector covers this backend.

cases.scenario: Worker error payload contains scoped capture borrow
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedErrorPayloadV1: a scoped capture borrow cannot leave its child inside an error payload. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q500] carrying 'an error payload requires own<Buffer>', at the raise that writes it rather than at the join. An accepted Linux control is the same program whose worker owns its payload, so the refusal is keyed to the borrowed capture and not to the raise form. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.scenario: Parent `?` bypasses a live sibling task
cases.semantic_profile: Actual scoped-copy task source checking: a second spawn with immediate ? has a dynamic failure edge leaving the first live handle, and rejects with Q600 ScopeBusy. The separate joined_sibling.qcore control joins the first task before creating the second; Linux checking/reference execution accepts it with both children joined. The rejected case executes parser/type checker only. No resource capture, sibling recovery handler or native execution of the rejected program is claimed.

cases.scenario: In-scope handler joins siblings before rethrow
cases.expected: Accept with all result obligations accounted
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1: an in-scope second-creation error handler joins the first child, drops its returned Buffer and rethrows the bound payload-free SpawnError. Four native/reference scenarios cover success, allocation failure and each creation failure with exact buffer/environment identities and join-before-reclamation checks. Omitting the sibling join or returned-buffer drop rejects at Q600. Owned error payloads, loans, arbitrary handlers, worker allocation and native refinement proofs remain open.

cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 lowered onto the unedited CheckedMutexInvariantV1 checker: two lexical critical sections over one mutex generation and one declared footprint, on one Linux thread. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, check, independent certificate recheck, C11 emission, and a run of the emitted C under ASan/UBSan/LSan whose stdout agrees line for line with interpret_mutex_program over the checked event list. `cfg` is unassessed because this route has no CFG stage at all. One thread, one target, one compiler invocation: not evidence about contention, scheduling, publication or the C memory model. DeclaredFootprintShape and InvariantPredicateDeclared are carried premises, and source-to-trace refinement is unproved in both Rust and Lean.

cases.scenario: Two different mutex identities allegedly guard the same payload
cases.expected: Reject without a valid composite protocol
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1: a second `mutex guards` over an already protected footprint is refused at Q617 FootprintAlreadyProtected, so no composite protocol is admitted; the exact ordered cascade [Q617, Q600 UnknownMutex] is pinned. The disjoint_payloads control declares two generations over two disjoint payloads and is accepted, so the refusal is keyed to the shared payload rather than to the number of mutexes. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; the accepted control compiles through the Linux-only emission path, which is what evidence_target records. No composite or nested protection protocol, lock ordering, or post-creation protection growth is established.

cases.scenario: Guard is moved to a child or unlocked by another thread
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card T03-F's bounded task composition: a child task written inside a critical section can lexically name the creator's guard, and acting through it is refused at Q612 WrongGuardAffinity; the exact ordered cascade [Q612, Q600 JoinWhileGuardHeld] is pinned, so the refusal is shown not to have released the guard the creator still holds. Both halves of the scenario execute: the case uses the creator's guard (`read buf with g`), and the child_unlocks control unlocks it (`close g`), refusing identically, so affinity is keyed to the acting task and not to the operation. The own_acquisition control is accepted: the same child takes its own acquisition of the same generation and the creator reads after the join. Only parser and type_checker execute; cfg is unassessed because this route emits from a checked event list and has no CFG stage. No native evidence: the accepted control is multi-task and this backend emits one thread, so it is published checked with c_source: None, and evidence_target records the Q500 host gate rather than a compiled or executed run.

cases.scenario: Typed error leaves a temporarily broken mutex invariant
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1: a typed-error exit taken with the invariant open is refused at Q614 InvariantOpenAtErrorExit, with the exact ordered cascade [Q614, Q619, Q600, Q600, Q600] pinned so the refusal is shown not to have released the guard. The restored.qcore control closes the invariant before raising the same error and is accepted, which is the scenario's `unless restored` half. Q613 and Q614 stay distinct codes: the error path is attributed separately from the normal path, and the Lean theorem typed_error_exit_obeys_the_normal_release_rule proves both exits obey the same release rule. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; the accepted control is Linux-gated. The invariant predicate has no runtime representation and stays the InvariantPredicateDeclared premise.

cases.scenario: Guard-derived borrow escapes critical section
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1: a guard-derived borrow still live at its critical section's end is refused at Q615 GuardBorrowEscape, with the exact ordered cascade [Q615, Q619, Q600, Q600, Q600] pinned. Two escape mechanisms execute: this one, and the escaped_borrow control, where naming the borrow binder after its block fails at Q013 unknown name because the binder is body-local; Q013 is recorded as name resolution and deliberately not relabelled as a concurrency verdict. The released.qcore control takes the same borrow, reads through the guard and drops it inside the section, and is accepted. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; the accepted control is Linux-gated. This profile refuses task creation outright, so a borrow cannot travel to a child here at all: no claim is made that a guard is unmovable in a future profile that admits tasks.

cases.scenario: Mutex destroyed with outstanding handle borrower/waiter
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card T03-F's `wait NAME;` form: an announced acquisition a child never performs blocks the generation's destruction at scope exit, refused at Q619 NonquiescentMutexDestruction with the exact ordered cascade [Q619, Q600 NonquiescentDestruction, Q600 OutstandingMutex, Q600 OutstandingWaiter] pinned; every entry after the first shows the refused destruction left the generation, the protected resource and the waiter outstanding rather than quietly destroying one of them. RegisterWaiter had no source form before T03-F, which is why this case was unmappable. The performed control has the announcing task perform the acquisition, withdrawing the announcement, and is accepted. Only parser and type_checker execute; cfg is unassessed (no CFG stage). No native evidence: `wait` is in the emission-refused set, so the control publishes with c_source: None and evidence_target records the Q500 host gate only. This is the model's waiter bookkeeping, not a blocking-acquisition or deadlock claim.

cases.scenario: Join while a guard is held
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card T03-F's bounded task composition: a child task created and joined strictly inside a critical section is refused at Q600 JoinWhileGuardHeld, and the cascade is exactly one entry long because the empty child body is well formed and nothing else is disturbed. The joined_outside control moves the identical block one statement past the section's end and is accepted, so the refusal is keyed to the join landing while a guard is held. This is the unedited T02 checker rule: T03-F declined to widen it, so a join strictly inside a guard is a refusal in this profile rather than a feature. Only parser and type_checker execute; cfg is unassessed (no CFG stage). No native evidence: the accepted control is multi-task and publishes with c_source: None; evidence_target records the Q500 host gate only.

cases.scenario: Lock order cycle in optional rank mode

One shared 4096-byte allocation read by two tasks
cases.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: two workers each declare `read page;` for the one `let page = share 4096;` cell, so the lowering names one cell identity and the checker's shared entry union counts 4096 once; the published epoch peak is 4096 + (1024 + 1024) + (512 + 2*128) = 6912. The mapping asserts every nonzero axis of the published certificate, not merely that the epoch checked. The two_cells control declares a second distinct 4096-byte cell that both workers read and measures 8192, so the union counts identities and not readers; the repeated_entry control names the same cell twice in one worker and is refused at Q630 rather than deduplicated. DeclaredTaskFootprints, DeclaredRuntimeOverhead, DisjointSharedStorageCells and NoScheduleModel are carried unchanged on the certificate: nothing here imports a footprint from C, from an allocator or from a run.

cases.scenario: Concurrent incremental peaks 3072 and 5120 bytes
cases.expected: Bound at least 8192 plus modeled overhead
cases.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: two independent workers declare `peak 3072;` and `peak 5120;`. Every assignment of phases to independent tasks is an admitted configuration, so the peaks are summed rather than maximized: the published concurrent private peak is 8192 and the epoch peak is 8192 + (512 + 2*128) = 8960, at least the summed peaks plus the modeled overhead. Two controls straddle the summed figure with the same two peaks — an allocation of 8192 is admitted and 8191 is refused with the ordered cascade [Q637, Q638] — and a maximized reading would have called 5120 the peak and admitted both, so the refusal is what makes the summing falsifiable. The overhead figures are a declared premise; a `measured RUNS` suffix in their place is Q640.

cases.scenario: Child returns allocation and finishes early
cases.expected: Allocation remains live in completion capsule
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1: a real worker allocates a Buffer and returns it into its completion record. The native adapter forces worker-body completion before creation returns and checks that the original allocation and environment remain live at join entry. Parent join transfers generation 4294967297, which must be consumed and dropped. Unconsumed or undropped results reject at Q600. The earlier sequential transferred-payload control remains separately executed. General memory-peak accounting, owned graphs, loan returns and native refinement remain open.

cases.scenario: Child credit splits total more than original credit
cases.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: two children each declare `credit 6144 effort 100;` out of an epoch that declares `bound 8192 effort 1000;`. Each child's own demand fits its own credit, so no per-task check refuses it; the granted total 12288 exceeds the 8192 allocation and the exact ordered cascade is [Q637] CreditsExceedAllocation on the memory axis. The control splits the same total within it (4096 + 4096 = 8192) and is admitted with granted_credits.memory = allocation.memory = 8192, so the refusal is keyed to the sum and not to the split.

cases.scenario: Concurrent work bound used as wall-clock bound
cases.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: a well-accounted epoch additionally writes `bound effort as latency;`, asking for its work bound as a completion time. The driver derives and independently rechecks the bound first and only then puts the claim to the profile's own epoch_wall_clock_bound, which always refuses: the exact ordered cascade is [Q639] WallClockUnavailable. The control is the same epoch without the claim, admitted with work_total on the effort axis = 800 and NoScheduleModel on the certificate, so a consumer cannot drop the premise and read the total as a finish time. There is no core count, queueing or preemption anywhere in this profile.

cases.expected: Old capability cannot authorize new identity
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1 Buffer lifetime identity: two successful root allocations are separated by real munmap/mmap at the same numeric address using MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE.
